source_refs.note: 1.1.2 Operations on Complex Numbers, definitions (i)-(iv) (book p. 2); PDF 7-7.

blocks.text: To develop the algebra of complex numbers, we state a few definitions. The symbols \(a, b, c, d, k\), where used, represent real numbers.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Why these rules? Treat \(i\) like a letter in algebra and collect like terms: real parts with real parts, imaginary parts with imaginary parts. The only new fact you use is \(i^2 = -1\).
In multiplication, the term \(i^2bd\) becomes \(-bd\). That is why the real part of the product is \(ac - bd\) (with a minus sign) and not \(ac + bd\).
Subtraction is defined as adding the negative: \(-(c + id) = -c - id\). Both parts change sign.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Division is not in this list. To divide by \(c + id\) we multiply the top and bottom by its conjugate \(c - id\), because \((c + id)(c - id) = c^2 + d^2\) is real. You will see this in 1.1.4 (Example 2).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Add or subtract real parts and imaginary parts separately.
2. \(k(a + ib) = ka + ikb\): a real number multiplies both parts.
3. Multiply like two brackets in algebra and replace \(i^2\) by \(-1\).
4. \((a+ib)(c+id) = (ac-bd) + i(ad+bc)\).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.text:
In subtraction, changing only the first sign: \((a+ib)-(c+id) \ne (a-c)+i(b+d)\).
In multiplication, forgetting \(i^2 = -1\) and writing the real part as \(ac + bd\).
Multiplying only the real parts and the imaginary parts: \((a+ib)(c+id) \ne ac + ibd\).
